text:
sam: Quick RFC follow-up — proposal for a small runtime compatibility gateway that normalizes route semantics across hosted / dedicated / private deployments. Goal: single adapter surface so rollouts + fallbacks behave identically.

devon: sg. can you paste the minimal config sketch? curious how latency vs cost signals get encoded.

sam: sketch below. it sits as a thin shim in front of the matchmaker and emits hints for the runtime (prefer/penalize/fallback). it's intentionally small to avoid a lot of extra RPCs.

```yaml
# runtime-compat-gateway config (proto sketch)
gateway_version: v0.3.0
compat_matrix_source: model_catalog
default_ttl_seconds: 300  # cache TTL for capability checks
rules:
  - match: tenant == "*"
    prefer: ["region:us-west-2", "tier:dedicated"]
    penalties:
      latency_ms: 20
      cost_usd_per_token: 0.0001
    preserve_pinning: true

signal_order:
  - static_capabilities
  - recent_probe_failures
  - runtime_health
```

aline: q: how do we detect an "incompatible" model variant? entirely static from catalog, or also live probes?

sam: two signals. prefer static capability matrix for perf and determinism; fall back to quick probe failures for staged rollouts. probe only when model is newly onboarded or during canary.

maria: concern: extra hop adds ~2-4ms. can we keep p99 SLA?

devon: we should inline most rule evaluation into the route resolver. gateway only does heavy checks when capability data missing. so common path is zero extra RPCs — just cache lookup.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary started on cluster us-west-2/edge-3 — runtime-compat-gateway v0.3.0

julie: need telemetry tags: `gateway.version`, `compat_reason`, `fallback_type`, and a counter for "preserved_pin" cases.

rick: cache invalidation model? TTL vs event-driven?

sam: TTL + invalidation events. default TTL 5m, but when registry webhook signals model change we emit invalidation for impacted keys. under heavy churn we can reduce TTL to 30s via config.

aline: rollback plan?

sam: auto-fallback header: `X-Runtime-GW: disabled`. canary weight controlled by router. also have an ops runbook to flip gateway feature flag globally. snippet: 

```text
runbook: 
- check canary metrics (p50/p95/p99 + error rate)
- if regressions: set header via edge-layer config: X-Runtime-GW=disabled
- scale down canary weight to 0 over 2min
- notify infra oncall
```

maria: ACK. i'll own unit/integration tests around tie-breakers + preserve pinning. will add a fuzz harness for policies.

devon: edge-case: tenant pinned to a quantized variant that's not in capability matrix. gateway must preserve explicit pinning, only override when tenant policy explicitly allows.

julie: i'll add dashboard tiles: mismatches by tenant, fallback count, avg added latency, and percent of preserved_pin cases.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary traffic 30% now, no errors in last 15m :thumbsup:

sam: decision summary: ship v0.3.0 shim with TTL cache + model-registry webhook for invalidation; inline rule evaluation into resolver to avoid RPCs on hot path; preserve tenant pinning by default; add telemetry and runbook.

sam: action items: @maria tests, @julie dashboards, @devon integration hooks (resolver + gateway), @aline update runbook + docs, @rick confirm model-registry webhook schema. will merge the PR after fixes, target EOD.

devon: noted. i'll also add a small opt-out header for customers who must bypass gateway for compat reasons.

julie: will add Grafana panels and an alert for >1% fallback rate over 5m.

sam: thanks all. i'll post the RFC diff and lightweight API proto in #eng-runtime later today."
